reason: The bottom-right graph matches the source pixels and is correct under the standard isothermal, isobaric, spontaneous closed-system interpretation: dG/dt remains nonpositive and damped oscillations approach zero. However, the problem states only that the system is closed; fixed temperature and pressure, absence of non-expansion work, equilibration, and oscillation of dG/dt itself are additional conditions. The Lean development proves the classification only with these conditions, including a directly assumed continuous rate_tends_to_zero field, so unconditional passed status is not justified.

coverage.evidence: Original PDF page 18 contains question 2.7, while blank answer sheet A2-6 on PDF page 24 shows the six choices. Direct inspection confirms that only the bottom-right curve oscillates entirely below zero with a decaying envelope toward zero. The six graphFeatures entries match the pixels, and satisfies_constraints_iff_bottomRight exhausts all constructors. gibbsDerivative_nonpositive correctly derives the derivative sign from antitonic Gibbs energy. The continuous selection theorem is nevertheless conditional on antitonicity, oscillation of the Gibbs rate, and its convergence to zero; the last two are structure fields rather than consequences proved from the printed problem.

unsupported_assumptions: The system is maintained at fixed temperature and pressure and performs no non-expansion work, allowing Gibbs energy to be treated as nonincreasing.
The closed reaction relaxes to equilibrium so that its continuous Gibbs-energy derivative tends to zero; ContinuousFixedTPClosedOscillatoryEvolution assumes this directly.
The statement that the reaction is oscillatory entails that dG/dt satisfies the submitted RealRateOscillates predicate; this connection is not derived from the source kinetics.
The discrete auxiliary model assumes Gibbs energy is bounded below and uses finite differences as an analogue of the requested continuous derivative.
